title: Local dimension lower bound for a polynomial quotient
statement: Let k be a field, m,t natural numbers, f : Fin t → MvPolynomial (Fin m) k, and assume the quotient by the span of the range of f is nontrivial and t ≤ m. Then at every prime p of its spectrum, ((m - t : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDimAt p.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00S8, lines 35834--35849, the lower-bound argument at maximal ideals and the Jacobson argument in Lemma 00OT.

proof.text: Every open neighbourhood of a prime contains a maximal ideal by the Jacobson property of a finite type algebra.
The localization at that maximal ideal has dimension at least m-t by the polynomial localization dimension theorem and the Noetherian height bound for the t generators.
The dimension at a closed point equals the local ring dimension, hence every neighbourhood has dimension at least m-t; taking the infimum gives the result.
